title: Callsite failure matrix — UX drafts and grooming
content:
Purpose:

This is a working doc for a compact console surface we are calling the "Callsite Failure Matrix". The idea: give engineers and SREs a lightweight, scannable matrix that helps them move from high-level error spike -> root cause hypothesis -> quick mitigation (replay/fallback). This doc captures UX sketches, grooming notes, initial acceptance criteria, and a small backlog for implementation + instrumentation.

Background / problem statement:
- Current Investigator/Workbench views are powerful but heavy; onboarding takes time in pager situations.
- Frequent triage flows: timeouts (client and upstream), 5xx from serving layer, and model-level failures (invalid logits, OOM at generation, tokenization errors). Teams need a quick heatmap of "where calls fail" across routes, models, and regions, plus a single-click path to replay with debug flags.
- We want something that sits on the Console homepage as a compact module, and expands into a focused triage modal (not a full-page redirect).

User journeys to support (core):
1) On-call SRE: sees a spike in 5xx rate. Opens Callsite Failure Matrix, filters to last 15 minutes, sees two routes accounting for 70% of 5xx; expands row to view sample payload and quick-replay. Replays against fallback model version; spike drops -> create incident note and pin rollback.

2) Product engineer: customer report of timeouts in Europe. Filters matrix by region, sorts by median latency, finds a route with high p95 and intermittent model OOMs. Uses "inspect tokens" action to view truncated token stream and KV-cache usage. Creates a ticket with sample request and slices.

3) Developer doing root-cause: wants to compare two invocations side-by-side (failed vs success). Uses multi-select in matrix to open diff view (request headers, prompt diff, model variant) and marks potential cause.

Wireframe / components (sketch notes):
- Top bar: quick filters (time range, region, route, model family, error class). Small pill counts for each filter.
- Matrix: rows = callsite (route or API key label), columns = error class buckets (timeout, 5xx-serving, 5xx-model, tokenization, rate-limit, fallback). Each cell shows: count, trend sparkline (small), and a severity dot (green/yellow/red). Cells are clickable to open a focused row panel.
- Row affordance: expand arrow reveals compact timeline (last 60s) and three actions: replay (with debug flags), open sample (shows request & truncated response), create ticket (pre-populated template).
- Focus panel (modal): left column = sample request + headers + prompt (collapsible long prompt with token count). Right column = quick diagnostics: last N error messages, stacktrace snippets (truncated), model runtime metrics (mem used, peak alloc, kv-hit-rate), and automatic hypotheses (derived from heuristics: e.g., "likely OOM: peak memory > 90% on host X").
- Diff mode: show two samples side-by-side; highlight differing prompt segments and model params (temperature, max_tokens).
- Small colored badge for "known issue" if this callsite matches a recent incident tag or linked rollback.

Heuristics / instrumentation needed (short):
- Error-class bucketing at ingestion: must tag events at router level with explicit reason field (timeout-upstream, timeout-client, model-oom, kv-cache-miss, etc.). Backfill where possible.
- Capture a lightweight sample for each unique callsite + error-class every 5 minutes (bounded retention).
- Track p50/p95/p99 latencies and per-callsite memory/alloc traces if available.
- Provide a standard JSON snippet for quick-replay API (route id, model id/version, debug flags, seed).

Backlog (initial grooming items):
- [P1] Matrix proto: build server-side aggregated endpoint (RINF-4682); UI list + cell sparklines. (2w)
- [P1] Row expand panel modal + sample viewer (includes token-truncate UX). (1w)
- [P2] Quick-replay integration with sandboxed debug model (opt-in). (1.5w)
- [P2] Diff mode MVP for manual comparison (UI only). (1w)
- [P3] Automatic hypotheses (heuristic engine) and link to incidents. (2w)
- [Tech debt] Event tagging standardization across router <-> serving runtime. (todo: infra task)

Acceptance criteria (first MVP):
- Matrix shows aggregated counts for time windows (15m / 1h / 24h) and cell-level sparklines that match backend aggregation within 5%.
- Row expand must surface at least one sample request and the last 3 error messages with timestamps.
- Quick-replay button triggers a sandboxed run and returns status (queued/ok/error) within 10s for small prompts.
- Filtering by region / route / model works and preserves selection when expanding rows.
- Basic telemetry: view-open, row-expand, replay-click must be emitted as events for later analysis.

Design tradeoffs and open questions:
- Where to store samples? Keeping full sample bodies in primary logs is expensive. Proposal: store truncated samples (first 4k chars) and a pointer to full logs in S3 with TTL=7d.
- Security: samples can contain PII. We should run a scrubber job (regex + allowlist) before showing in UI. Who owns policy? Security team + product to decide.
- Replay scope: should replay by default be limited to non-production models? We need guardrails and a permission model.
- Auto-hypotheses correctness: risk of misleading heuristics; MVP should mark hypotheses as "suggestions" with provenance data.

Mockup notes for front-end handoff (mini-spec):
- Colors: use existing Console palette; severity red = #E23D3D, warning = #F6A623, ok = #1F9D74.
- Sparklines: 24px high, monotone line, overlay small dot on latest value.
- Accessibility: keyboard navigable rows; aria-labels for cells include route + bucket + count.
- Mobile: collapse matrix into list-of-cards for small screens; prioritize route + top error.

Next steps (this sprint):
- Design: Ethan to mock two variations (compact matrix vs stacked list) by 2024-09-10.
- Backend: Arjun to prototype aggregated endpoint + sample retention plan; sync with infra on tagging by 2024-09-12.
- Security: Rachel to draft scrubber rules and a short policy doc for samples by 2024-09-15.
- Demo: Prepare a 5-minute demo for triage guild review (target 2024-09-24).

Notes / discussion log (brief):
- 2024-09-03 slack: initial idea posted in #console-design, positive reaction re: quick-replay.
- 2024-09-05 meeting: team prefers matrix to be a home-page module (low friction). Concern about cost of storing samples raised by infra.

Unresolved items to decide at grooming:
- Exact retention window for samples (7d vs 30d) and storage budget.
- Which error classes to show by default (we should keep list short; propose: timeout, serving-5xx, model-failure, tokenization, rate-limit).
- Permission model for replay action.
